summary: The increment has real substance: a daily market lock with fail-closed corrupt-file handling, an O_EXCL-based alert cooldown with atomic reservation, a multiprocess mutual-exclusion test, CI success on 75b1024, and HEAD/tree parity between VPS and origin. It cannot be approved. (1) Three-way parity fails. The local Windows porcelain shows 5 modified tracked files and 1 untracked test file, so the shipped artifact is not the code under development. The matching content hash comes from the git index and does not prove the working tree matches. (2) One of the three objective items, the S05 Director Plan NameError fix, has no diff shown, no test, and no runtime invocation, so it is unverified. (3) The live state contradicts the claimed guarantees. scan_count=15 exceeds the verified MAX_SCAN_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT=10. 27 suppressed alerts in about 2h indicate a re-invocation storm that the cooldown is hiding rather than fixing (Rule 139). The 'Live Daily Quota Guard Skip Check' targets EN even though an EXHAUSTED_TODAY lock exists for the current VN date, so it shows the guard was not applied. (4) The EN_2026-10-16 lock was written at 17:42:21Z (00:42 VN), 7 seconds before the forensic suite's timestamps, which suggests the evidence collection consumed tomorrow's production quota on /var/vf/locks. (5) The cross-platform lock relies on os.kill(pid, 0). On Windows this calls TerminateProcess and kills the target process, which directly contradicts the module's Windows-safe mandate. (6) Scope bleed and coverage regression: an adversarial test suite was deleted, synthetic alignment was removed from CI, historical audit records were deleted, and there are large hhtech_reasoner/boss_orchestrator rewrites tied to AVF-VOX-001. (7) Required ffprobe evidence is absent and the cron-log forensics do not show the 06:21 VN incident.

Fix the stale-reclaim TOCTOU. Reclaim by atomically renaming the stale lock to a unique tombstone and verifying the token before deletion, or move to fcntl.flock/msvcrt.locking on a persistent lock file. Add a test where two reclaimers race on one stale lock.
Remove the absolute 60s age-based reclaim of live holders, or add a heartbeat (periodic mtime touch) for the holder.

Explain and fix scan_count=15 > MAX_SCAN_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT=10. Print the effective resolved cap at runtime and assert it in test_candidate_loop_halts_at_max_scan_candidates against the real B1 entrypoint.
Make run_trend_pipeline.py dry-run evaluate the daily lock and report 'EN: SKIP (EXHAUSTED_TODAY)'. Define whether --market overrides the lock (it should not without --force) and test it.
Find the source of the roughly 27 B1 re-invocations in 2h (cron schedule, vps_runner retry, or orchestrator loop) and stop it at the source. Show the crontab, systemd units, and log timestamps.

Isolate forensic and test runs from production state (VF_STATE_DIR pointed to a temp directory). Restore or recreate the EN_2026-10-16 lock state per operator decision, and confirm with the user before modifying /var/vf/locks.

Restore tests/vox/test_align_adversarial.py, or provide an equivalent replacement suite proving Rule 120 adversarial alignment coverage. Justify the ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_ALIGNMENT removal in a separate scoped commit.
Restore the deleted audit records (round9.md, round10.md), or move them to an archive path tracked in git. Do not delete audit history.

Split out the hhtech_reasoner.py, boss_orchestrator.py, SKILL.md, and visual_audit.py changes into their own task, or provide diffs, tests, and a Rule 138 caller trace (list all 20 callers, not just a count).
Provide raw cron log lines covering the original 06:21 VN incident and a post-fix cron window showing exactly one B1 Telegram message per market per VN day.
Provide the full untruncated ci_neighbor_tester.py output and the full pytest suite (tests/) exit code on the VPS, not only the 4 targeted files.
Provide ffprobe JSON for a rendered episode, or obtain explicit user waiver that this increment produces no video artifact.

component_reviews.analysis: On Windows, os.kill(pid, 0) is not a liveness probe. CPython maps non-CTRL signals to TerminateProcess(handle, sig), so a stale-lock check can kill a live sibling process. On Linux, PermissionError (EPERM: the process exists but is owned by another user) is an OSError subclass and is misread as dead_pid=True. Stale reclaim has a TOCTOU race: process A reads stale lock L1, process B reclaims and creates L2, then A unlinks L2 by path, which breaks mutual exclusion. The 60s absolute-age fallback reclaims locks from live long-running holders because the holder never refreshes mtime. Release reads then unlinks non-atomically. Five 'except OSError: pass' blocks swallow errors silently (empty-except pattern) with no log. The fail-closed timeout and the token-on-create are correct.

The broad 'except Exception' covers both IO and parse errors. Quarantine to .corrupt.<ts> is sound in intent, but these files accumulate without bound. The retention policy test (tests/unit/test_corrupt_retention_policy.py) exists only as an untracked local file, so that hardening was not shipped. Live state shows suppressed_since_last=27 between 15:41:51Z and 17:42:21Z. The throttle works, but the root cause, repeated B1 invocation, is masked.

The visible contract is reasonable: VN-date keying, IN_PROGRESS TTL, a COMPLETED/EXHAUSTED_TODAY taxonomy, corrupt input failing closed, and a force override via flag or env. The 6-process ProcessPoolExecutor test asserting exactly one winner is good adversarial evidence. Open issues: the file has uncommitted local modifications; the implementation diff past the truncation point was not provided for line-level review; and the EXHAUSTED_TODAY records show scan_count=15 against a cap of 10. Either the cap is not enforced on that path, or an env override is active and was not disclosed.

This is a primary objective (the NameError fix), yet the evidence contains no diff hunk, no unit test, no py_compile output, and no live stage invocation (Rule 127). 19 changed lines with zero verification. The fix is unproven.

The 'Live Daily Quota Guard Skip Check' prints 'Target markets would be [EN]' while EN_2026-10-16.json (the current VN date at collection time) is EXHAUSTED_TODAY. Either the explicit --market override bypasses the guard, or dry-run skips the guard. In both cases the evidence contradicts the claim. Commit 3125580 'relax viability evidence gate' loosens a factual-integrity gate (Rule 130) without the before/after falsifiability data being shown.

Coverage is solid for state transitions and concurrency. test_detects_completed_episode_on_disk patches Path.is_dir and Path.iterdir at class level. This affects every Path in the module, and the mock makes the real on-disk detection path untested even though a real temp directory was already created. test_force_flag_bypasses_lock mutates os.environ directly instead of using monkeypatch.setenv.

Deleting a 210-line adversarial suite and removing ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_ALIGNMENT from CI is outside this task's objective. It reduces boundary coverage (Rule 134), and no replacement was shown proving that Whisper word-level alignment (Rule 120) is still adversarially tested. A green CI after removing tests is weaker evidence.

Historical audit records (round9.md, round10.md) were deleted, which destroys audit provenance (Rule 137 spirit). An AVF-VOX-001 audit JSON was committed under this task. hhtech_reasoner.py had 1160 lines changed and boss_orchestrator.py 845 lines with no diff, no test, and no blast-radius trace (Rule 138). These changes belong to a different task and break atomic code-ification (Rule 124).

VPS HEAD = origin/main = local HEAD = 75b1024, and the VPS porcelain is clean. The local Windows porcelain is dirty: M alert_cooldown.py, M daily_market_lock.py, M opus55_supervisor_gate.py, M tests/test_ghost_scan_adversarial.py, M tools/ghost_scan.py, ?? tests/unit/test_corrupt_retention_policy.py. Parity is not established.

Ghost scan exit 0 is valid for the VPS, but ghost_scan.py itself has uncommitted local edits, so the verified scanner is not the one being developed. The ci_neighbor_tester output is truncated at the start ('7:42:28,604'), and logs for Blocks 1.0–3.0 are absent. Only the summary lines are visible.

Section 3 promises '06:21 VN conflicting Telegram messages & B3 crash' but extracts one line at 08:29:42 and '0 TOPICS PRODUCED'. It shows neither the original incident nor its absence after the fix. ffprobe JSON is missing entirely, which is a mandatory element of the 10/10 policy. Only the 36 targeted unit tests were run. A full pytest suite exit code was not provided.

observations: The EN_2026-10-16 EXHAUSTED_TODAY lock (pid 70545, 17:42:21Z = 00:42 VN) and last_suppressed_utc 17:42:21Z are 7 seconds before the forensic suite's 17:42:28 log lines. The evidence collector very likely ran a live B1 crawl against production /var/vf/locks and burned the next VN day's quota. Forensic collection must be isolated from production state.

scan_count=15 on both exhausted locks against MAX_SCAN_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT=10 means the verified constant is not the effective runtime bound. Constant verification without effective-value verification is not falsifiable.

27 suppressions in about 2 hours means B1 is being re-triggered roughly every 4–5 minutes. The cooldown keeps this from reaching Telegram. The underlying retry loop is a symptom that should be fixed at its source (Rule 139). The daily lock should short-circuit before any scan, and the alert path should never be reached.

The matching content hash (git ls-files | sha256sum) hashes the path list and does not cover working-tree bytes. It cannot detect local modifications. Parity evidence should hash blob contents (git ls-files -s or git write-tree on a clean tree) and assert empty porcelain on all three nodes.
The commit log mixes TASK_1792069373 and AVF-VOX-001 work ('Round 17 forensic punchlist'). The increment is not single-purpose, which makes the audit boundary ambiguous.

The design choice to fail closed (done=True) on a corrupt lock is correct for quota protection. It needs an operator-visible alert, otherwise a single corrupt file silently halts a market indefinitely.
